purpose: Trial of absence, crash and return: one member is killed mid-meeting and later relaunched (resume-fork of its session), and a second process claims a seat already held. Two agenda questions from specimens-2026-11-03.md; outcomes not acted on.

seats.vantage: harness security: what a permission rule admits, and what else the same pattern could let through
identity reliability and the record: tools like vsect need to know which agent acted, and that only works if the identity prefix is never refused
every other Claude session on this machine: global settings reload live into all of them, so a global change is felt by sessions that never agreed to it

agenda.title: Keep or remove the global allow rule Bash(export CC_AGENT=*)?
agenda.brief: Facts (from the agent-identity README, 2026-11-02): a global PreToolUse hook rewrites every Bash command a Claude Code agent runs to begin with `export CC_AGENT='<key> parent=... type=... depth=... src=agent-identity-hook/2'; `, so tools (vsect, git trailers) can read which agent acted. Claude Code's permission check runs on the rewritten command, so an allow rule `Bash(export CC_AGENT=*)` was added to ~/.claude/settings.json. Measured: without it, in default permission mode the export needed approval and ordinary allowed commands were refused. The README's argument that it is safe: the rule matches only the export; a command after it is judged on its own (a test `touch` still needed approval); `export CC_AGENT=$(...)` substitution is refused by the harness's export parser. Not verified: how two PreToolUse hooks that both rewrite Bash combine; what the TUI permission prompt shows. The rule was added by the implementing agent with the refactor lead's approval; it now waits on Joseph. Move what you would recommend to him (keep, remove, or keep with conditions).

agenda.title: Who should check a plan like the vsect maturation plan: one independent reviewer from another model family, or a council?
agenda.brief: From specimens-2026-11-03.md (reply 1, item 9): a draft plan for maturing a record-keeping tool (vsect) is waiting for review, and it is open whether one independent reviewer from another model family or a council should check it. The estate's experience: the agent that authors a result is never the one that verifies it; independent checkers found defects in roughly 43% of landings that integrators re-checking their own work had confirmed 116 of 116. Move what you would recommend.
